context.body: God says it is not good for the man to be alone; animals are formed and brought to him for naming, yet no corresponding helper is found.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The repeated declaration that creation is good is interrupted by the phrase “not good,” centered on human aloneness.
observations.label: Not good to be alone: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Forming · bringing · naming visible within its account or reuse of creation.
observations.label: Not good to be alone: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: God identifies what is not good · The man · Living creatures · Forming · bringing · naming · Good creation · human aloneness

payload.posture: Read Genesis 2:18–20 as its own human focus creation setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places Good creation · human aloneness inside this creation setting without making it a conclusion for every creation passage.
